claims.text: Interface pinning can be used as an alternative to full ab initio thermodynamic integration for calculating melting properties.
Interface pinning is equivalent to a two-phase coexistence method.
The proposed method can accurately calculate the melting temperature of refractory materials.
The proposed method can accurately calculate the entropy of fusion of refractory materials.
The proposed method can accurately calculate the enthalpy of fusion of refractory materials.
The proposed method can accurately calculate the volume change at the melting point of refractory materials.
The proposed method significantly reduces computational expense relative to full thermodynamic integration using ab initio molecular dynamics.
Interface pinning or two-phase coexistence dynamically forms and stabilizes an interface between solid and liquid phases.
A stabilized solid-liquid interface facilitates direct extraction of free-energy differences.
Direct simulation of coexisting solid and liquid phases drives the system toward a metastable equilibrium.
The metastable equilibrium permits extraction of the free-energy difference between the solid and liquid phases.
The alternative method requires considerably shorter simulation times than full thermodynamic integration.
The computational-cost reduction could be approximately one order of magnitude.
The method's effectiveness depends on accurately capturing interface dynamics.
The precision of the method against experimental benchmarks for refractory materials has not been fully validated.
The general applicability of the method across diverse refractory materials has not been fully established.
